newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end firm on portfolio corrections.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end firm on portfolio corrections.

text.p: Surging interest in property and over the counter (OTC) stocks helped Singapore share prices close above the 2,200 level on Monday as portfolio imbalances were corrected, dealers said.
"We're seeing a rotational interest in Singapore, rather than a flood of brand new interest," one dealer said.
Nevertheless, Singapore's benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) was buoyant, closing up 10.94 points at 2,205.69 on heavy volume of 194.87 million shares.
Singapore's over the counter (OTC) market was running strong on an upturn on the Kuala Lumpur stock exchange, which has been "underweighted for some time", according to one dealer.
The UOB OTC index closed up 6.47 points at 1,227.50 on Monday, fuelled by gains on property stocks such as Land and General and Renong.

Debut share, interior design firm, Nobel Design, saw 64.83 million units traded, ending the day at Singapore $0.535 against an offer price of S$0.33. Thai communications firm, Total Access Communications, gained U.S. $0.40 to close at US$6.85.
A positive rating of six Singapore banks by ratings agency Standard & Poor's had almost no impact on prices, dealers said.
